structural: The structural obligations in `requirements.sdk.outlines.OutlineAttachment` are: a `#[non_exhaustive]` public struct `OutlineAttachment` with public fields `kind: AttachmentKind` and `span: Span`. It also needs `pub fn new(kind: AttachmentKind, span: Span) -> Self`, plus `Clone` and `Debug` implementations. An alternative with private fields, no `non_exhaustive`, or no `new` would break the stated signature and type. The `Clone` and `Debug` clauses are covered the same way.

The supplied roots cover all of these:
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/contents.rs#struct[OutlineAttachment]` declares the struct with `#[derive(Clone, Debug)]` and `#[non_exhaustive]`. Its public fields are `kind: AttachmentKind` and `span: Span`. This covers the type, field and trait-implementation obligations.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/contents.rs#impl[OutlineAttachment]/fn[new]` has the signature `pub fn new(kind: AttachmentKind, span: Span) -> Self` and returns `Self { kind, span }`.

Both roots carry the `{impl}` marker.

The cited `requirements.sdk.outlines.attachments.span` is context only. It describes what value the span holds, which is observable behavior of the language providers that produce attachments. It is not a structural obligation of this type.

behavioral: The only behavioral obligation is that a language provider can build an attachment from `kind` and `span`, and that both values are kept. The span semantics belong to the cited `requirements.sdk.outlines.attachments.span`.

- `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[custom_attachment_spans_are_checked_against_the_original_snapshot]` is marked `{test}` for `OutlineAttachment`. Its `Custom` language provider (the `outline` method of `impl[Custom/OutlineLang]`) builds attachments with `OutlineAttachment::new(AttachmentKind::Other("marker".into()), *span)`.
- The test asserts that `attachment.kind == AttachmentKind::Other("marker")`. It also asserts that `&snapshot.text()[attachment.span] == "é"`. Together these show `new` stores both fields and that the public `kind` and `span` fields are readable.
- The same test covers the cited span rule. It slices the original snapshot at the span and checks the whole construct. It also checks that spans splitting a character, lying outside the snapshot, or extending past the item are rejected.
- `outline_constructors_preserve_fields_and_replace_attachments` also calls `OutlineAttachment::new`, but it isn't marked. That is only redundant coverage, not a gap.
- `#[non_exhaustive]`, the field declarations and the `Clone` and `Debug` derives are structural and type-level. They have no conditional or transformation of their own, so they need no behavioral test. `public_api.rs#fn[public_exports_match_the_appendix]` covers the public export inventory.

pub fn new(kind: AttachmentKind, span: Span) -> Self;
Each attachment's `span` is a half-open byte range in the original file
snapshot, even when the caller has selected a nested item. Slicing that
snapshot at the span yields the complete source construct, including its
delimiters. Repeated occurrences have their own spans.
